# Row-Bot Docs Full Text

Concatenated public documentation for Row-Bot.

## Row-Bot Documentation

Route: /docs/

A complete public user guide for installing, configuring, and using Row-Bot end to end.

# Row-Bot Documentation Row-Bot is a local-first AI workbench for people who want provider-aware models, parent-led agents, durable documents, memory, tools, workflows, design, code help, integrations, and voice in one controllable system. Run it as a desktop application or a private authenticated server; this guide explains installation, Docker deployment, owner access, the main interface, settings, and every explicit external route. These pages describe Row-Bot 5.0.0, the release represented by this source tree. ## Start Here - [Getting Started](/docs/getting-started/) explains the install path, first launch, and setup choices. - [Row-Bot Interface](/docs/app-shell/navigation) tours the sidebar, Home, a conversation and its details card, panels, the terminal, the K command palette, Buddy and Settings. - [Home: Overview](/docs/home/overview) explains the first page: the Ask box, what needs you, live status and recent work. - [Chat](/docs/chat/) explains conversations, composer controls, attachments, model selection, approvals in place, tool results, and the conversation library. - [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls) explains model-specific effort, thinking toggles, token budgets, and provider-default fallback behavior. - [Settings](/docs/settings/) explains every settings page and what each choice changes. - [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/) explains the Agents dialog, goals that keep going until done, delegated agents, and recovery. - [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access) explains invitations, sessions, Tailscale, LAN, HTTPS proxies, and browser-local voice. - [Docker And VPS Operations](/docs/operations/docker/) explains the official container, persistent data and secrets, backup, upgrade, and rollback. - [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use/) explains the opt-in native desktop tool, setup, live controls, and safety boundaries. ## Feature Guides - [Workflows](/docs/guides/workflows) for repeatable background work and scheduled agents. - [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls) for choosing the supported reasoning depth of the active model without changing models. - [Designs](/docs/designer/) for decks, documents, landing pages, mockups and storyboards in a conversation's Design panel. - [Code Folders](/docs/developer/) for binding or cloning a folder from a conversation and working on it in the Developer panel. - [Knowledge](/docs/knowledge/) for local memory, durable document ingestion, graph review, and background organization. - [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use/) for target-window automation in native Windows and macOS applications. - [Phone And Native Desktop](/docs/mobile-native/) for the same owner product on a phone and in the native desktop app. - [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access) for owner invitations, Tailscale, LAN, SSH, Docker, HTTPS proxies, and remote browser voice. - [Docker And VPS Operations](/docs/operations/docker/) for the official image, hardened Compose, credentials, backup, upgrade, rollback, and recovery. - [Monitor](/docs/monitor/) for kept health checks, one-click fixes, activity, history, and logs. - [Insights](/docs/home/insights) for what Row-Bot noticed and the proposals it prepared for your review. - [Skills Hub](/docs/skills/) for browsing, enabling, creating, and reviewing skills. - [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills) for automatic external-tool discovery, per-task skill selection, compatibility mode, and safety boundaries. - [Channels](/docs/integrations/channels), [MCP](/docs/integrations/mcp), and [Plugins](/docs/integrations/plugins) for integrations. - [Extend Row-Bot](/docs/extending/) to choose safely between Skills, Custom Tools, plugins, MCP, channels, and accounts. - [Operations, Data, And Recovery](/docs/operations/) for backups, restore, updates, repair, uninstall, and diagnostic sharing. - [Voice and Buddy](/docs/voice-and-buddy/) for speech input, Talk, Dictate, read-aloud, and Buddy's native drag-to-undock desktop overlay. ## How To Read These Docs Each major page explains what the feature is, where to find it, the important controls, a common workflow, what is saved, privacy and safety implications, and troubleshooting. Screenshot captions describe the product UI so you can connect the text to what you see in the app. ## References Use [Reference](/docs/reference/) when you need tables of tools, providers, settings pages, channels, skills, MCP servers, plugins, storage, or approval behavior. The guided pages should be your first stop; the reference pages are for lookup.

## Getting Started

Route: /docs/getting-started/

Install Row-Bot, complete first launch, and learn the first choices that matter.

# Getting Started Start here if you are new to Row-Bot. You only need three things for a useful first session: the app installed, one working model path, and a basic understanding of where Row-Bot stores local data. ## The Short Path 1. Install Row-Bot from the release package for your platform. 2. Launch the app and answer **How should Row-Bot think?** 3. Choose one model path: local Ollama, a hosted provider, a subscription account, or a custom endpoint. 4. Send a first chat message. 5. Open Setup Center or Settings later when you are ready for documents, workflows, designs, code folders, channels, MCP, plugins, Skills, Buddy, or voice. ## Important Concepts - **Local app** means Row-Bot runs on your machine and opens a local desktop or browser window. - **Data directory** means the folder where Row-Bot keeps conversations, memories, documents, settings, workflows, logs, designs, code folder records, skills, plugins, and local integration state. - **Model provider** means the service or local runtime that supplies a model. Ollama is local; API and subscription providers usually use the internet. - **Tools** are actions Row-Bot can take, such as reading files, searching documents, using a browser, running commands in a code folder, or sending through a channel. - **Approvals** ask you to approve or deny sensitive actions before Row-Bot proceeds. They wait until you answer. ## Pages In This Section - [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation) - [First Launch](/docs/getting-started/first-launch) - [Row-Bot Interface](/docs/app-shell/navigation)

## Installation

Route: /docs/getting-started/installation

Install Row-Bot from a release package or run it from source with clear next steps.

# Installation For ordinary use, install Row-Bot from the latest release package for your operating system. Running from source is useful for contributors, testers, and people who want to inspect or modify the app. ## Install From A Release 1. Download the latest Row-Bot release for Windows, macOS, or Linux. 2. Run the installer or unpack the archive. 3. Launch Row-Bot from the Start Menu, Applications, app launcher, or the provided command. 4. Answer **How should Row-Bot think?** to choose your first model. The installed app starts a local Row-Bot process and opens the UI in a desktop window or browser, depending on your platform and launch preference. If the usual port is busy, Row-Bot chooses another local port. ## Run From Source Use the source path if you are developing Row-Bot or testing changes: 1. Clone the repository. 2. Create a Python environment. 3. Install uv and sync the locked Python dependencies with `uv sync --locked --all-extras --group test`. 4. Install the docs-site dependencies only if you are working on documentation. 5. Run the app entry point from the repository. `requirements.txt` is a generated pip export from `uv.lock` for installer compatibility. It is available as a fallback for environments that cannot use uv, but source dependency changes should be made in `pyproject.toml`. Source runs use the same local data concepts as the packaged app. Keep test data separate from personal data when experimenting. ## Local Data Directory Row-Bot stores local app data under the active Row-Bot data directory. This includes conversations, memories, model/provider metadata, workflows, designs, code folder records, documents, logs, skills, plugins, Buddy assets, channel settings, and MCP settings. Advanced users can set `ROW_BOT_DATA_DIR` before launch to use a separate data directory for testing or portable runs. Do this before starting the app, and remember that Row-Bot will treat that folder as the active local data store for the whole process. ## After Installing Continue to [First Launch](/docs/getting-started/first-launch). You can finish optional setup later from the Setup Center and Settings. The standard desktop install stays on local loopback. To connect another trusted computer or phone, finish local setup first and then follow [Remote Access And Server Mode](/docs/operations/remote-access). For a headless or container deployment, read that guide before publishing a port or creating the first owner invitation.

## First Launch

Route: /docs/getting-started/first-launch

Answer "How should Row-Bot think?" to choose your first model, then finish the rest at your own pace in Setup Center.

# First Launch The first time you open Row-Bot, it asks one question: **How should Row-Bot think?** Your answer connects one working model, which becomes the default for new conversations. Everything else can wait for Setup Center. Every desktop, source, and official Docker install uses the same first launch. ## How Should Row-Bot Think? Pick one of three cards. You can add other providers later. | Choice | What it means | Tradeoffs | | --- | --- | --- | | **On this computer** | Private and free, with Ollama. | Needs Ollama and a downloaded model; larger models need more memory and disk space. | | **With my subscription** | ChatGPT, Claude or Grok. | Signs in to an account you already pay for and follows that provider's terms. | | **With an API key** | OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter and more, or your own endpoint. | Needs an API key and internet access; the provider bills per use and receives the prompts you send it. | - **On this computer** walks you through it: **Install Ollama** if it is missing, **Start Ollama** if it isn't running, **Download a model**, then **Pick a model** from the models on this computer. - **With my subscription** lets you choose ChatGPT, Claude or Grok and sign in. - **With an API key** lists the recommended providers first and the rest under **More providers**. Choose one, paste its key, and pick a model. Advanced users can add an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, such as LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI, LiteLLM or SGLang. After you pick a model, Row-Bot sends it a short test message. A local model can take a minute to load the first time. If the model doesn't answer, choose **Try again** or **Choose another model**. If Row-Bot finds Hermes Agent or OpenClaw on this computer, it then offers to bring that assistant's memories, persona and skills along. Choose **Import from ...** or **Not now**; you can import later from **Settings Data**. Choose **Set up later** to look around first. Home then stops opening setup for the rest of this window, and Overview reminds you to choose how Row-Bot thinks. ## Setup Center Setup Center is where you finish the rest whenever you like. Open it from Overview's **Finish setup** card or from the command palette (**Setup Center**). 1. **What would you like to use?** Pick any of: chat assistant, research and documents, workflow automation, designs, code, messaging channels, or local and private AI. Recommended areas move to the top. 2. **Continue setup** lists each area with one button that goes where it is set up: Models, Knowledge, Workflows, Designer (starts a design in a chat), Developer, Channels, Accounts, Tools & Skills, MCP & Plugins, Voice, and a Final Check that opens Monitor to run the diagnosis. 3. Each area's **** menu marks it done or skips it. Areas Row-Bot can check, such as a connected model, tick themselves. The links at the bottom import from Hermes or OpenClaw, or set up private knowledge search. ## Install Private Knowledge Search Row-Bot can search your memories and documents by meaning with **Mixedbread Embed Large v1**, a separate local model for semantic memory and document search. It is a 675 MB download from Hugging Face and is not the model that writes chat responses. Install it from **Settings Documents** (Setup Center's **Set up private knowledge embeddings** link goes there). Under **Index health and maintenance**, **Search model files** offers **Download** for the first install, **Retry** to load an already cached model again, and **Repair** to replace a damaged download. Files go into Row-Bot's private cache; documents and memories are not uploaded, and normal recall stays offline after the download. Docker keeps this cache in its named `/data` volume. Until it is installed, Row-Bot continues with bounded lexical and graph fallback, so chat and memory do not stop working. Rebuild the document and memory vectors after changing the search model. ## Privacy, Cost, And Credentials Local model runs can stay on your computer. Hosted, subscription, realtime voice, web search, account, channel, MCP, and plugin features can contact outside services when configured and used. Enter provider keys and account sign-ins only through first launch or the relevant Settings page. Cost depends on the provider or service you choose. ## Troubleshooting - If Row-Bot can't find Ollama, install or start it, then check again from the same card. - If a provider connects but no models appear, refresh it in Settings Providers. - If the test message fails, try again or choose another model; a small local model may need a minute to load. - If the private knowledge model download fails, check internet access to Hugging Face and try **Download** again later. - If you skipped setup, open Setup Center from Overview or the command palette.

## Models And Providers

Route: /docs/configuration/models-and-providers

Configure providers, discover models, choose defaults, and pin quick model choices.

# Models And Providers Providers are where models come from. Models are the specific choices you use in conversations, workflows, designs, code folders, voice, and other Row-Bot surfaces. To understand what leaves the app, when tools run, and where approvals fit, read [How A Request Runs](/docs/concepts/request-lifecycle). ## Recommended Setup Order 1. Open Settings -> Providers (or answer **How should Row-Bot think?** at first launch). 2. Connect one provider path. 3. Refresh provider health. 4. Open Settings -> Models. 5. Refresh the catalog. 6. Choose the **Brain** model, and Vision, Image and Video models if you want those jobs. 7. Pin the models you use most. 8. Test in a chat. ## Choosing A Provider Path Use local Ollama for local-first privacy and no provider billing. Use an API provider for strong hosted models. Use a subscription account when you already have the supported provider account. Use a custom endpoint for advanced local or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible runtimes. ## Choosing Models Keep at least one everyday chat model and one stronger tool-capable model pinned. For code folders, designs, workflows, and complex tools, choose a model that can handle tool calls and enough context. For models with exact reasoning capabilities, Row-Bot exposes a per-thread [Reasoning control](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls) with only the efforts, toggle, or token-budget choices that model supports. Provider default remains available as the compatibility-safe option. For Ollama, Row-Bot prefers explicit tool-calling metadata, then the daemon's reported capability list. A reported `tools` capability enables agent use even for a model family newer than Row-Bot's maintained fallback catalogue; an explicit capability list that omits `tools` remains authoritative. Family fallbacks are used only when the daemon provides no capability metadata. ## Troubleshooting - If a provider connects but has no models, refresh Models. - If a model fails with tools, choose a tool-capable model. - If an Ollama model is unexpectedly excluded from agent use, refresh the local catalogue and inspect the capabilities reported by the installed Ollama daemon. - If a custom endpoint fails, check base URL, model name, API compatibility, and context window.

## Row-Bot Interface

Route: /docs/app-shell/navigation

Find your way around Row-Bot: the sidebar, Home, a conversation and its details card, panels, the terminal, the command palette and Settings.

# Row-Bot Interface Row-Bot has one window with three parts: the **sidebar** on the left, the main area in the middle (Home, a conversation, the conversation library, or Settings), and, in a conversation, the **panels** for its designs and code folders on the right, with the **terminal** docked underneath when you open it. ## The Sidebar - **New chat** starts a conversation. Its **** starts a chat with one of your favourite agents, or **All agents...** opens the Agents dialog. - **Home** opens the Home tabs: Overview, Workflows, Knowledge, Monitor and Insights. See [Home](/docs/home/). - **Agents** shows your favourite agent profiles as icons (one click starts a chat with that agent) and **All agents**, which opens the Agents dialog with the whole profile library. See [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/). - **Conversations** lists your conversations, pinned ones first. The icons beside the heading filter by type: All, Chats, Designs, Code and Workflows. A conversation's row shows when it is replying, waiting for approval, or has agents working. - A row's pin button keeps it at the top; its **** menu renames it, exports it as Markdown or PDF, or deletes it. - **Show all** lists every conversation in the sidebar; **Conversation library** opens the full library to search, filter, export and clean up. See [Chat](/docs/chat/#find-export-and-clean-up). - The **attention indicator** at the bottom appears only when something needs you: waiting approvals (with **Approve** and **Deny** in place), problems (opens Monitor), or an available update (opens Updates). - **Buddy** sits above **Settings**. In the native Windows and macOS apps, drag Buddy itself out of the sidebar to undock its desktop overlay. See [Settings: Buddy](/docs/settings/buddy). - **Settings** opens the settings pages. See [Settings](/docs/settings/). Collapse the sidebar to a narrow rail with its toggle; the rail keeps New chat, Home, Agents, the attention indicator, Settings and Buddy as icons. ## A Conversation The conversation's header shows its name (click it to rename), **Find** to search the conversation, **Share or export**, and **Conversation details**. The **details card** beside the conversation lists what the conversation is **Working on** (its designs and code folders), its **Outputs**, its **Goal**, and the **Agents** it started. A delegated agent's own conversation shows the way back to its parent in the header. See [Chat](/docs/chat/). ## Panels And The Terminal A design opens in a **Design panel** and a code folder in a **Developer panel**, beside the conversation. Open them from the details card or the header's **Open panel** menu; drag the divider to resize. See [Designs](/docs/designer/) and [Code Folders](/docs/developer/). In the desktop app, the **terminal** opens docked under the conversation with the terminal button, **Open panel Interactive terminal**, or Ctrl+`. See [Tools, Approvals, And Terminal](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#interactive-terminal). ## The Command Palette Press K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux), or the search button at the top of the sidebar, to open the command palette. Type what you want in your own words: - **Requests** such as "connect a model", "phone", "connect telegram", "add mcp server", "install a skill", "change model", "connect gmail" or "back up" go straight to the exact place it is done. Words can come in any order. - **Conversations and messages** are found by title and by words in their messages. - **Commands** open Home tabs, the conversation library, Setup Center, Settings or the Agents dialog, and toggle the sidebar, the details card or the terminal. Each shows its shortcut. - **Settings pages and rows** open at the exact row. - **Switches** flip a setting in place, showing its current state, with **Undo** afterwards: for example "turn off shell", "turn on developer tools", the browser tool, Dream Cycle, learning new skills, or the habit tracker. "dark mode", "light mode" and "follow the system appearance" change this device's appearance. - **Agents** and **workflows**: "Chat with ..." starts a chat with an agent; "Run ..." runs a workflow. Enter runs the top result only when it matches what you typed; otherwise choose a result with the arrow keys. ## Keyboard Shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | | --- | --- | | K / Ctrl+K | Open the command palette | | O / Ctrl+Shift+O | New chat | | . / Ctrl+. | Show or hide the conversation details card | | Ctrl+` | Open or close the terminal | | / | Find a setting, on a Settings page | | Enter / Ctrl+Enter | Approve the focused approval | | Z and Z / Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z | Undo and redo in the Design panel | | Esc | Close the palette, a menu or a dialog | ## On A Phone Or Tablet On a narrow screen, the sidebar becomes a drawer opened from the top bar, panels open as full-screen sheets, and the conversation header's **** menu holds Find, Conversation details, Share or export, the panels and the command palette. See [Phone And Native Desktop](/docs/mobile-native/). ## What Is Saved Conversations, their names, models, profiles, workflows, knowledge, settings and logs are saved in the local Row-Bot data directory. Panel sizes, the terminal's height, favourite agents and appearance are remembered on each device. ## Troubleshooting - If a conversation is missing from the sidebar, use **Show all**, the type filter, or the conversation library's search. - If a panel looks stale, close and reopen it from the details card. - If a button is disabled, check the related Settings page and Monitor for readiness messages.

## Home: Overview

Route: /docs/home/overview

Start from Home Overview: ask Row-Bot anything, answer what needs you, see live status, and pick up recent work.

# Home: Overview Overview is the first page Row-Bot opens. It answers three questions at a glance: what needs you, what is running, and where you left off. Everything on it opens the place where the work actually lives, so you can act without hunting through tabs. ## Where To Find It Choose **Home** in the sidebar. Overview is the first of the five Home tabs: Overview, Workflows, Knowledge, Monitor and Insights. Until a default model exists, opening Row-Bot opens [first launch](/docs/getting-started/first-launch) instead. ## Ask Box And Quick Starts - **Ask Row-Bot anything, or describe what to make...** starts a new chat with your text. Use **Add files in a new chat** to attach files first, then **Start chat**. - **New design** and **New code folder** set up a design or a code folder and open it in a new chat with its panel beside it. See [Designs](/docs/designer/) and [Code Folders](/docs/developer/). - **New workflow** opens the workflow editor on the Workflows tab. - **Continue "..."** reopens your most recent conversation. ## Needs You **Needs you** comes first and counts what is waiting for you: - **Approvals** from any conversation, workflow or delegated agent show **Approve** and **Deny** right in the card, with how long each has waited. Open the conversation or workflow when you want the full context first. - **Interrupted agent work** offers **Resume** or **Dismiss**. - **Failed workflows** offer **Run ... again**. - **Health checks that need attention** carry their one-click fix, such as restarting a stopped channel, reconnecting an account, choosing a model, or checking again. See [Monitor](/docs/monitor/). - **Finish setup** appears while Setup Center still has steps; hide the reminder once you are done. When nothing waits, the card says you're all caught up. ## Live Status The status strip shows four tiles, each opening its tab: | Tile | What it shows | | --- | --- | | **Agents** | Agents working in your conversations right now. | | **Workflows** | What is scheduled next and today's runs. | | **Memory** | A small picture of your most connected memories and what is new this week. | | **Health** | The latest Monitor checks, which run by themselves. | ## Recent Work - **Continue where you left off** shows recent conversations as cards, with pinned ones first and a mark on any that is replying, waiting for you, or was interrupted. - **Since yesterday evening** is a timeline of what ran: workflow runs, finished agents, Dream Cycle runs and new memories. - **Learned this week** lists subjects Row-Bot saved to memory, and a current insight with **Open Insights**. See [Home: Insights](/docs/home/insights). ## What Is Saved Overview stores nothing of its own. It reads your conversations, workflows, approvals, memories and Monitor checks, and every action runs through the same reviewed command as the place it comes from. ## Troubleshooting - If Overview opens Setup instead, finish choosing a model or choose **Set up later**. - If a tile reads **Unavailable**, refresh the page; Monitor shows whether the service behind it is healthy. - Approving from Overview is the same decision as approving in the conversation. Open the conversation first when the request is not obvious from its title.

## Chat

Route: /docs/chat/

Use Row-Bot conversations: the composer, models, attachments, tools, approvals in place, the details card, names, and the conversation library.

# Chat A conversation is the main place to work with Row-Bot. It can stay a simple chat, or use memory, documents, tools, approvals, attachments, skills, voice, agents, goals, designs and code folders. ## Start A Conversation - Choose **New chat** in the sidebar (O / Ctrl+Shift+O), or type into the Ask box on [Home Overview](/docs/home/overview). - Use the **** beside **New chat**, a favourite agent in the sidebar, or **Chat with ...** in the command palette to start with an agent profile. A new conversation is named from the first words of your first message straight away, then gets a short name of its own after the first reply. Click the name in the header to rename it; a name you choose is kept. ## The Conversation - **Header**: the conversation's name, **Find** to search it, **Share or export**, and **Conversation details** (. / Ctrl+.). - **Transcript**: your messages and Row-Bot's replies, each with a small speaker mark (your Buddy's picture for Row-Bot), plus tool steps, how long Row-Bot thought, charts, images, generated media, approval cards and the agents a turn started. - **Composer**: type the next request. Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. **Send** becomes **Stop** while Row-Bot replies. ## Composer Controls - **Model** chooses the model for this conversation. See [Model Picker](/docs/chat/model-picker). - **Thinking** appears beside the model only when that exact model exposes supported reasoning choices. See [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls). - **Approvals** sets how actions are reviewed in this conversation: **Ask** (approve each consequential action), **Block**, or **Auto**. - The **+** menu (**Add files and more**) holds **Attach file**, **Add resource...** (a design or code folder), **Skills...**, **Agent profile**, and **Mode**: **Agent** uses tools and agents, **Chat only** answers without tools. - **Skill chips** above the composer show the skills in use, including default ones; removes one from this conversation. - **Voice** buttons use Dictate or Talk when voice is set up. ## Attachments Attach files with **+ Attach file**, by dropping them on the conversation, or by pasting. Each file shows as a small tile above the text: pictures show a preview, other files their type, name and size. Tiles show upload progress and offer **Retry** if an upload fails. You can keep adding files while others upload; **Send** waits for them. Click a tile to preview it, or to remove it. ## The Details Card **Conversation details** sits beside the conversation on a wide screen. It shows: - **Working on**: the designs and code folders bound to this conversation. Choose one to open its panel, or unbind it from its **** menu. **Add resource** binds another. - **Outputs**: images and videos the conversation made, linked to where they appear. - **Goal**: the conversation's goal and its progress, or **Set a goal**. See [Profiles, Goals, And Agents](/docs/profiles-goals-agents/). - **Agents**: the agents this conversation started, each with its status, **Message** and **Stop**. Its **** menu offers **Manage conversation**, **Manage browser** and **Delete conversation**. ## Approvals When Row-Bot needs your decision, an approval card appears in the conversation with **Approve** and **Deny**. Approvals wait until you answer, and they also show in the sidebar's attention indicator, on Overview and in Buddy, so you can decide from wherever you are. See [Tools, Approvals, And Terminal](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal). ## Beginner Workflow 1. Start a new chat. 2. Choose a model that is ready for chat. 3. Ask one clear question or task. 4. Attach files only when the task needs them. 5. Review any approval before allowing Row-Bot to act. ## Power Workflow 1. Start a chat with the agent profile for the kind of work. 2. Pick a stronger tool-capable model. 3. Bind the design or code folder you are working on. 4. Set a goal when the work needs several turns. 5. Let Row-Bot use tools, but approve file writes, browser actions, shell commands, account actions, channel sends, MCP calls, and plugin tools deliberately. ## Continue From The Buddy Overlay In the native Windows and macOS apps, drag Buddy from the sidebar onto the desktop for a compact view of the selected conversation. Its composer shares that conversation's saved draft, model, tools, approval mode, and active response. Simple approvals can appear in the overlay; open the full thread for complex approvals, attachments, transcript history, tool traces, model controls, Talk, or Dictate. See [Settings: Buddy](/docs/settings/buddy). ## Find, Export, And Clean Up - **Share or export** in the header opens the conversation's actions: change its **Name**, **Pin** it to the top of the sidebar, or **Export** it as **Markdown** or **PDF**, then **Save export** to choose where the file goes. - A sidebar row's **** menu exports or deletes one conversation too. - **Conversation library**, at the end of the sidebar's list, lists every conversation. In the library, **Search titles and messages**, filter by type (All, Chats, Designs, Code, Workflows), and select conversations. The selection bar at the top pins or unpins them, exports them as Markdown or PDF, or deletes them; **Clear selection** (Esc) starts again. Exported files go to Row-Bot's Exports folder; **Show in folder** opens it. Deleting a conversation stops its running work, then removes its messages, drafts, attachments, media, tool sessions, workflow state and agent state after you confirm. Bound designs and code folders remain. Developer worktrees with changes and sandboxes with unimported work are kept and reported, so deletion does not discard source work. Export anything you need before confirming because deletion cannot be undone. ## What Is Saved Conversation names, messages, model choices, per-model reasoning selections, approval mode, profile, attachments copied into Row-Bot-managed storage, and tool results are saved locally. External providers receive prompt content only when you choose their models. ## Privacy And Safety Local model runs can stay on your machine. Hosted models, web search, browser actions, account tools, MCP servers, plugins, and channels can send data outside the app when configured and used. Row-Bot should not insert secrets into chat; enter credentials only through Settings or the provider's sign-in flow. ## Troubleshooting - If Row-Bot cannot answer with the current model, choose a more capable model in the picker. - If the Thinking control is missing or a saved choice resets, read [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls#troubleshooting). - If attachments are ignored, check that their tiles finished uploading and that they are relevant to the prompt. - If a tool is unavailable, check the composer's **Mode**, the conversation's agent profile, approval mode, and Settings. - If an external tool is enabled but not selected automatically, use a more specific request or review [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills). - If a reply is stuck, press **Stop**, then retry with a narrower prompt.

## Model Picker

Route: /docs/chat/model-picker

Choose a conversation's model from one list across local, subscription, pay-per-use and custom providers, and troubleshoot missing models.

# Model Picker The model picker in the composer chooses which model answers in the current conversation. It is where provider setup becomes visible in day-to-day use. ## Where Models Come From Models appear after Row-Bot discovers them from a connected provider or local runtime: - Local Ollama models come from the Ollama service running on your computer. - Subscription models come from a ChatGPT, Claude or Grok account you signed in to. - Pay-per-use models come from a provider connected with an API key in Settings Providers. - Custom endpoint models come from the compatible endpoint details you provide. - Models you pin in Settings Models appear first. The same list is used everywhere a model is chosen: the composer, and the Brain, Vision, Image and Video pickers in Settings Models. ## Using The Picker - **Search models** narrows long lists; **Recent** shows the models you used last. - Models are grouped by provider, each marked **Connected** or **Not connected**, and tagged with how they are paid for: **Subscription**, **Pay per use**, **Credits**, or **Local - free** (runs on this device). - A model that can't be used right now, for example because its provider is disconnected, shows as **Unavailable** with the reason. - **Chat only** marks models that can't use tools. - The choice applies to this conversation only; it doesn't change your default model in Settings Models. ## Choosing Well Use a smaller or local model for quick private chats. Use a stronger tool-capable model for workflows, designs, code folders, long context, or multi-step tool use. For local and self-hosted endpoints, prefer a context window large enough for Row-Bot's instructions and tool schemas. Reasoning choices belong to the exact provider-qualified model, not just its display name. After choosing a supported model, use the conditional Thinking control described in [Reasoning Controls](/docs/chat/reasoning-controls). ## Pinning Models Open **Settings Models**, find a model in the **Catalog**, and pin the ones you use often. Pinning doesn't create a new model; it puts an existing one at the top of every picker. ## Troubleshooting - If the picker says there are no models yet, choose how Row-Bot thinks in Setup, or connect a provider in Settings Providers. - If a model is missing, refresh the provider in Settings Providers, then refresh the catalog in Settings Models. - If a model shows as unavailable, read its reason; reconnecting its provider usually fixes it. - If a model appears but fails with tools, choose a model that isn't marked **Chat only**. - If custom endpoint models look duplicated, use the provider-qualified name.

## Reasoning Controls

Route: /docs/chat/reasoning-controls

Choose provider-aware reasoning effort, thinking toggles, and token budgets for the active Row-Bot model.

# Reasoning Controls Reasoning controls let you change how much supported models reason before answering without switching models. Row-Bot shows only choices that the exact provider-qualified model reports or that Row-Bot can identify from a maintained model route. ## Where To Find The Control - In every conversation, including those working on a design or code folder, the **Thinking** control sits beside the model picker in the composer. In narrow windows, the composer progressively compacts labels while keeping each icon paired with its own menu. - On a phone, the composer's controls fold into a smaller set of buttons; Thinking still appears next to Model when the selected model supports it. - In Chat or a connected messaging channel, use `/reasoning` to inspect the current choice and the valid choices for the active model. The control is intentionally absent when Row-Bot does not have exact, actionable reasoning capability data for the selected model. A generic model name or a provider-wide assumption is not enough. ## What The Choices Mean | Choice | Effect | | --- | --- | | Provider default | Sends no per-thread reasoning override and lets the provider or endpoint choose its normal behavior. This is the safest compatibility choice. | | Low, Medium, High, XHigh, or another effort | Requests one of the exact effort levels supported by the selected model. The list varies by model. | | On or Off | Enables or disables thinking only when that model exposes a true toggle. Models with mandatory reasoning do not offer Off. | | Token budget | Sets a positive reasoning-token budget within the minimum and maximum reported for that model. This appears only for budget-capable models. | More reasoning can increase latency and provider token usage. It can help with planning, coding, analysis, and multi-step tool use, but a higher setting is not automatically better for every request. ## Scope And Persistence A selection is saved locally for one thread and one exact provider-qualified model. Switching models does not apply an incompatible value to the new model. If you return to a model in the same thread, Row-Bot can restore that model's valid saved choice. Changing the global default model does not rewrite existing thread choices. Conversations working on designs and code folders use the same thread-scoped behavior as any other conversation. ## Slash And Channel Commands Run `/reasoning` with no argument to show the active setting and valid choices. Supported examples include: ```text /reasoning high /reasoning default /reasoning on /reasoning off /reasoning budget 4096 ``` Row-Bot validates the command against the active model. Unsupported efforts, toggles, or budgets are rejected without replacing the previous valid selection. Messaging channels use their conversation's active thread and model, so the setting remains isolated from unrelated chats. ## Providers And Custom Endpoints Row-Bot maps native reasoning controls for supported OpenAI and Codex, Anthropic and Claude Subscription, xAI, Google, Ollama and Ollama Cloud, OpenRouter, and compatible endpoint routes when exact capability data is available. Available models and choices can change as provider catalogs change; the control itself is the authoritative list for the selected model. For a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, open **Settings -> Providers**, edit or add the endpoint, then expand **Advanced -> Reasoning**. Keep **Reasoning mode** on Auto unless the endpoint's metadata is missing or wrong. Thinking budget, returned reasoning content, replay, and extra request JSON are advanced compatibility settings that apply to every model exposed by that endpoint. Enable replay only when the endpoint explicitly supports receiving preserved reasoning history. ## Responses And Compatibility Fallback When a provider returns reasoning content, Row-Bot can stream it separately and retain it as a collapsed **Thinking** section instead of mixing it into the final answer. If a provider rejects a valid-looking explicit reasoning choice before returning response content, Row-Bot retries once with Provider default, clears the rejected saved override, and shows a notice. Authentication failures, rate limits, timeouts, cancellations, and server failures are not silently retried as reasoning compatibility problems. ## Privacy And Safety The selected control is stored locally with thread settings, but hosted providers receive the resulting reasoning parameter and may bill for additional tokens. Reasoning content returned by a provider can contain sensitive intermediate material. Do not enable reasoning replay for a custom endpoint unless you trust that endpoint and understand its message format. ## Troubleshooting - **The control is missing:** confirm the active model is provider-qualified, refresh Providers and Models, and check that its catalog entry exposes exact reasoning capabilities. - **A choice disappeared after switching models:** choices are model-specific; inspect the new model's menu or run `/reasoning`. - **A saved choice reset to Provider default:** the provider rejected it or refreshed capability metadata no longer supports it. Read the notice, refresh the catalog, and choose from the current list. - **A custom endpoint returns reasoning in the wrong place:** review its Advanced Reasoning settings, especially returned reasoning content and replay. Keep replay off unless required. - **High reasoning is slow or expensive:** choose a lower supported effort, a smaller budget, or Provider default.

## Tools, Approvals, And Terminal

Route: /docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal

Understand Row-Bot tools and tool steps, approvals that wait until you answer, and the interactive terminal docked under a conversation.

# Tools, Approvals, And Terminal Tools are actions Row-Bot can take beyond writing text. They can search documents, read files, use a browser, run commands, work on designs and code folders, inspect knowledge, call MCP servers, use plugins, or send through channels. ## Progressive Discovery With the recommended Auto capability-loading mode, core tools remain available under the active profile while Row-Bot searches enabled MCP, plugin, Custom Tool, and channel tools only when a request needs them. This keeps large external schema catalogs out of unrelated prompts. Discovery does not widen permissions. The selected provider, Agent Profile, workspace policy, approval mode, and execution budget still apply. Live and reopened traces group results under the real integration name. See [Progressive Tools And Skills](/docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills) for the complete flow and the eager compatibility option. ## How Tool Use Appears When Row-Bot uses tools, the turn shows a tool step: what Row-Bot tried, what came back, and whether more action is needed. Open it for each call's details. Each result also records whether approval was needed, given or denied, so Row-Bot reports it truthfully. A denied action shows as skipped, never as done, and Row-Bot is told that it did not run. ## Approvals Approval cards appear when an action can change local files, run commands, contact external systems, use accounts, start servers, send messages, call MCP or plugin tools, or do something else that deserves review. The composer's **Approvals** control sets the mode for the conversation: **Ask**, **Block** or **Auto**. **Approvals wait until you answer.** They no longer expire after a set time; a workflow step that sets its own time limit still honours it. Each one shows how long it has been waiting. **Answer them where you are.** Every waiting approval, from this conversation, another conversation, a workflow or a delegated agent, shows with **Approve** and **Deny** in place: - in its conversation, as an approval card; - in the sidebar's attention indicator ("1 approval is waiting"), which opens the list; - in Overview's **Needs you** card; - in Buddy, including the desktop overlay; - in the channel a workflow or channel-started task came from, when that channel supports approvals. A floating notice also says when a new one arrives. An answer in one place resolves it everywhere. When a delegated agent needs approval, its parent conversation shows it too. The card may include a short reason written by the model, but Row-Bot's approval policy still decides whether the action is blocked, allowed, or waiting for you. Before approving, check: - What action is being requested. - What file, folder, account, channel, server, or provider is involved. - Whether the action can send data outside the app. - Whether the proposed command or file change matches your request. - Whether denying is safer until you inspect settings. Approving lets Row-Bot continue that action. Denying stops that action and returns control to the conversation. ## Interactive Terminal In the Row-Bot desktop app, a conversation can open a real interactive terminal docked at the bottom of the window. Open or close it with the terminal button in the header, **Open panel Interactive terminal**, the command palette (**Toggle terminal**), or Ctrl+`. - Type straight into it: colours, line editing, command history (the arrow keys) and Tab completion work as in your own terminal, and interactive programs answer. - **Stop** (Ctrl+C) interrupts the running command, **Clear** clears the screen, **Open in your terminal** opens your own terminal app, and **Close** hides the dock. Closing and reopening keeps the session and its scrollback. - Drag the divider to resize it; the height is remembered on this device. In a phone-sized window it opens as a full-screen sheet instead. - After the shell exits, **Start again** opens a new one. The terminal is for you: what you type runs as your own commands on this computer. Commands Row-Bot runs as tools still follow workspace boundaries, tool availability and approval mode, and appear in the conversation's tool steps. The terminal needs the Row-Bot desktop app: in a browser on this computer the dock says so, and other devices don't offer it. ## Common Workflow 1. Ask for a task that may need tools. 2. Let Row-Bot explain the intended action. 3. Review the approval card, wherever you see it. 4. Approve only if the action matches your intent. 5. Open the tool step to check the result. 6. Ask Row-Bot to summarize what changed. ## Troubleshooting - If no approval appears, the action may be read-only, allowed by the conversation's **Auto** mode, or blocked before running. - If a tool result is confusing, ask Row-Bot to explain the last tool call. - If the terminal says it needs the Row-Bot desktop app, open the conversation there; the button is not offered on other devices. - If you denied by mistake, ask Row-Bot to try again and review the next approval.

## Progressive Tools And Skills

Route: /docs/guides/progressive-tools-and-skills

Understand how Row-Bot discovers external tools and task-specific skills without loading every capability into every prompt.

# Progressive Tools And Skills Row-Bot can keep a large extension library enabled without sending every external tool schema and every skill instruction to the model on each turn. By default, it progressively discovers the capabilities that match the current request. ## How Tool Discovery Works Core Row-Bot tools that are permitted by the active Agent Profile remain available normally. Enabled external tools from MCP servers, plugins, Custom Tools, and channels are kept in a searchable catalog. In **Auto-select external tools** mode, Row-Bot: 1. Searches the enabled external-tool catalog when the request needs an integration. 2. Selects the matching tool without changing its underlying identity or provider contract. 3. Applies the same profile filtering, workspace policy, execution budget, prompt-injection handling, and approval rules as a directly bound tool. 4. Shows the real integration name in live and reopened tool traces rather than a generic invocation wrapper. Discovery does not enable disabled integrations, add credentials, or bypass an approval. If two capabilities conflict with a core tool name, Row-Bot keeps the core boundary intact. ## How Skill Discovery Works Skills are instruction packages, not executable permissions. Enabled skills can be searched when a request clearly matches their purpose. Row-Bot may then load the relevant skill for that task and show a **Using _skill_** receipt plus an active skill chip. Automatically loaded skills are scoped to the current task. Reopening the task restores its active skills, while a different parent task or child Agent keeps independent activation state. Up to five automatically selected skills are retained per task; pinned skills are managed separately. Loading an already active skill is a no-op and should not create a duplicate receipt. ## Parent And Child Boundaries Each child Agent receives its own profile, tool allow-list, approval mode, workspace policy, execution budget, and skill activation state. A child can use the skill discovery bridges when its runtime permits them, but loading a skill cannot grant a tool that its profile denies. Child skill choices also do not leak into the parent or a sibling child. Use **Row-Bot Status** inside a child run when you need to distinguish globally configured tools from the tool groups actually bound to that child. ## Auto And Compatibility Modes Open **Settings -> Tools -> Capability loading**: - **Auto-select external tools (recommended)** keeps the prompt compact and discovers enabled external integrations as needed. - **Load all external tools** is the eager compatibility mode. It sends every enabled external tool schema that survives the same provider and policy filters, which can use substantially more model context. Changing this setting does not alter tool enablement, credentials, approvals, or saved Agent Profiles. ## What You See In Chat - Skill discovery can show `skill_search`, followed by one **Using _skill_** receipt after a successful load. - External discovery can show a search step followed by a result grouped under the real integration name. - Reopened transcripts preserve the real external-tool label. - Direct tools in eager mode keep their existing labels and approval behavior. ## Troubleshooting - If no matching tool is found, confirm the integration is installed, enabled, healthy, and allowed by the active profile. - If a skill is not selected, confirm it is enabled and make the requested task specific enough to match its purpose. - If a child can see a tool in global status but cannot call it, inspect the child's profile-selected tool groups. Global availability is not the same as runtime access. - If a provider rejects a tool schema, try a compatible tool-capable model; discovery does not weaken provider schema validation. - Use eager mode temporarily when diagnosing an older provider or integration that expects direct external-tool binding. See [Tools Settings](/docs/settings/tools), [Skills Settings](/docs/settings/skills), [Skills Hub](/docs/skills/), and [Extensions And Trust Boundaries](/docs/concepts/extensions-and-trust) for related controls and safety boundaries.

## Profiles, Goals, And Agents

Route: /docs/profiles-goals-agents/

Manage agent profiles in the sidebar's Agents dialog, give a conversation a goal that keeps going until done, and follow the agents it delegates to.

# Profiles, Goals, And Agents These three features work together but solve different problems. An **agent profile** is a reusable role and policy. A **goal** is an objective a conversation keeps working toward, turn after turn. An **agent run** is one piece of delegated work, with its own conversation, status and result. For the mental model behind delegation and hand-offs, read [How Profiles, Goals, And Agents Work](/docs/concepts/profiles-goals-and-agents). ## Agent Profiles Open the **Agents** dialog with **All agents** in the sidebar's **Agents** section, **All agents...** under **New chat**'s ****, the Agents icon on the collapsed rail, or **Agent profiles** in the command palette. It lists every profile in groups (Everyday, Creative, Developer, your own profiles, and profiles from workspaces, plugins or imports), with **Search profiles** and a scope filter. Each profile row can: - **Pin to the sidebar**: pinned profiles become favourites in the sidebar's **Agents** section and under **New chat**'s ****, one click from a new chat; - **Start chat** with that profile; - **View**, **Duplicate**, and, for your own profiles, **Edit**, turn on or off, or **Delete**. **Create profile** describes a new role: its name, description and when to use it, instructions, capability (read only, write capable, or orchestrator), allowed tools and skills, context mode, workspace mode and approval mode. Keep the role narrow: describe the outcome, the sources it may use, and what it must not do. To use a profile in an existing conversation, choose it from the composer's **+ Agent profile**. Profiles do not grant capabilities by themselves. A selected tool must still be enabled, available, and allowed by the conversation's approvals. ## Goals A goal is useful when work needs more than one turn. Set it from the conversation's details card: under **Goal**, choose **Set a goal**, describe **What should this conversation achieve?**, and choose **Start goal**. Row-Bot starts at once and keeps going turn after turn; it stops for approvals and when it needs you. - **No turn limit by default.** Overnight and multi-day goals keep going while they make progress. Set an optional **Turn limit** or **Time limit (hours)** when you want one. A default turn limit for new goals is in Settings Models Limits for long work. - **Smart stop.** Row-Bot pauses the goal and says why when it stops making progress (no progress in the last 2 turns) or the same step fails 3 times. When a provider's usage limit stops a turn, the goal waits and continues by itself once the limit resets, if the provider says when. - **Survives restarts.** An active goal continues after Row-Bot restarts or the computer wakes, from its last saved turn, asking again for anything that needed approval. - **Visible usage.** The card shows the goal's state (Working, Continuing, Waiting for your approval, Paused, Needs you, Done or Stopped), the turn it is on ("Turn 7", or "Turn 7 of 30" with a limit), how long it has been running and the tokens it has used. - **Pause**, **Resume** and **Stop** control it. Stopping ends the goal; it does not delete the conversation or its evidence. Starting a new goal replaces the current one, and **Earlier goals** lists the ones before. ## Delegated Agents A conversation can delegate parts of its work to agents. Each agent works in its own conversation. - **In the transcript**, the turn that started agents shows a small stub for each one, with its icon, name and live status (working, waiting for you, done, failed or stopped). A failed agent's stub says why. Click a stub to open that agent's conversation. - **In the details card**, **Agents** lists them, live and failed ones first. **Message** sends an agent a note it reads at its next step; **Stop** ends its run. - **In an agent's own conversation**, the header leads back to the parent conversation. - **When an agent needs approval**, the request appears in the parent conversation and everywhere else approvals show. See [Tools, Approvals, And Terminal](/docs/chat/tools-approvals-and-terminal#approvals). - **If work was interrupted** before it finished, for example by a restart, the card and Overview's **Needs you** offer **Resume agent work** or **Dismiss agent work**. A completed agent's result is evidence for the parent, not automatic permission to write files, send messages, commit code, or publish. For coding work, a parent can assign an agent to an existing local folder. Row-Bot registers that folder as the agent's code folder and applies writer ownership to the resolved folder, not merely the process working directory. Agents assigned to distinct folders or worktrees can write in parallel; writers targeting the same folder wait and run serially. New runs also receive a checkpointed work budget. Settings Models **Limits for long work** shows the recommended steps per run, helper levels, helpers at a time, and the optional helper time limit. Extra agents wait in a first-in, first-out queue when capacity is full; changing a setting affects new runs, not work already in progress. If a run appears stuck, open its conversation to read its last update before stopping it. If several agents edit the same resource, give them distinct folders or worktrees, narrow their ownership, or run them sequentially. Keep consequential final actions with the parent and a human approval point. Row-Bot saves the parent's first continuation checkpoint when asynchronous delegation begins. If a child process outlives its launching shell or the app restarts, resume repairs only genuinely unanswered tool calls with an interruption marker, then wakes the parent from durable child results. It does not replay previously executed work. If a checkpoint cannot be repaired safely, the run remains stopped for review. Repeated model-and-tool states are detected before a run can loop indefinitely. The fourth identical no-progress state is blocked; a fifth ends the run cleanly with a durable reason. Reaching a configured work limit also finalizes the run instead of leaving it marked as active. ## What Is Saved Profiles, goals, agent runs, edges, progress, results, and evidence are stored in the active local data directory. Favourite profiles are remembered on each device. Provider prompts still follow the privacy terms of the model route selected for each run.

## Workflows

Route: /docs/guides/workflows

Create, run, schedule, edit, deliver, and troubleshoot Row-Bot workflows.

# Workflows Workflows are repeatable Row-Bot tasks. Use them for things you want to run again: a morning brief, inbox follow-up, document digest, research check, report draft, or channel delivery. A **reminder** is a simpler kind that just tells you something at a chosen time. For the execution model behind schedules, persistent runs, approvals, and delivery, read [How Background Workflows Run](/docs/concepts/background-workflows). ## Where To Find Workflows Choose **Home**, then the **Workflows** tab. Overview's **New workflow** quick start and the K command palette (**Run ...**) also reach them. ## The Workflow List - Each row shows the workflow's name, when it runs next, its last runs, and small tags for its steps, profile and approvals. **Auto approvals** stands out. - **Run** starts the workflow at once, in one click. The row then shows its live state and **Stop**. - **Enable** or **Disable** turns the workflow's schedule on or off. - **Edit** opens the workflow editor. - The row's **** menu opens **Run history**, **Edit workflow steps**, **Workflow settings** or the workflow's conversation, and can duplicate or delete the workflow. - **Search workflows**, the filter and **Select workflows** help with long lists. - **Delivery defaults** choose the external channels every workflow also sends results to, unless a workflow chooses its own. The app always shows the result. ## Create A Workflow 1. Choose **New workflow**. The editor opens on the page, as editing does. 2. Give it a name, an icon and a short description, and choose **Workflow** or **Reminder**. 3. Write the **Steps**: what Row-Bot should do first, then what next. Each step can use the previous step's output; drag steps, or use the arrow keys, to reorder them. 4. Choose **When it runs**: manually, at a date and time, or repeating (every day, weekdays, chosen days, every few hours or minutes, or a custom cron expression). 5. Choose **Send results to**: follow your defaults, choose channels only for this workflow, or keep results in the app. 6. Under **Model and approvals**, pick an **Agent profile** and **Approvals**: **Ask before actions**, **Block actions**, or **Auto, within the profile**. 7. Save, then **Run** it once and review the result. ## Advanced Workflows - **Edit workflow steps** opens the step editor, with a builder and a step graph. Besides prompts, steps can be conditions, approvals, running another workflow, delegating to an agent, waiting for agents, and notifications. - **Workflow settings** chooses the model, whether runs reuse one conversation, a concurrency group, and the trigger: manual and scheduled runs only, **When another workflow completes**, or **Webhook (HTTP POST)**. A webhook trigger creates a private secret when you save; download its configuration and keep it private. ## Approvals In Workflows An approval step, or an action that needs approval, pauses the run until you answer. It waits as long as needed unless that step sets its own time limit. Answer it from the sidebar's attention indicator, Overview's **Needs you**, the workflow's conversation, Buddy, or a channel that supports approvals; an answer in one place resolves it everywhere. While a run waits, that workflow's next scheduled run is skipped and says so. ## What Is Saved Workflow definitions, schedules, run history, delivery defaults, and status are local Row-Bot data. Results may be sent to channels only when configured and selected. ## Safety Avoid workflows that send messages, write files, start servers, or call external systems without a review point. Use approvals for actions that can affect files, accounts, channels, MCP servers, plugins, or external services. Remember that **Run** starts at once, including any delivery outside the app. ## Troubleshooting - If a workflow does not run on schedule, check that it is enabled and that an earlier run isn't still waiting for approval. - If delivery fails, check the selected channel and its Settings page. - If a run waits for approval, answer it from the attention indicator or Overview. - If results are too broad, split the workflow into smaller steps.

## Designs

Route: /docs/designer/

Create decks, documents, landing pages, app mockups and storyboards with Row-Bot, and edit, present, share and export them in a conversation's Design panel.

# Designs Row-Bot can make visual work with you: decks, documents, landing pages, app mockups and storyboards, with your brand's colours, fonts and logo, charts, and generated images or video. Each design belongs to a conversation and opens in that conversation's **Design panel**, beside the chat, so you can ask for changes and see them land. ## Start A Design - **Ask in a chat:** "Make a five-slide deck about our spring workshop." Row-Bot creates the design, and the finished design opens in the panel by itself when you are not typing. - **Home Overview New design** sets one up and opens it in a new chat. - **In a conversation**, open the composer's **+** menu, choose **Add resource...**, then **Design**. Choose **Create new** (the type, an optional name and brief, a template and canvas, and **Draft it now**) or **Open saved** to bring an existing design into this conversation. The conversation's details card lists it under **Working on**; choose it there, or from the header's **Open panel** menu, to reopen the panel. ## The Design Panel - **Preview** and **Edit** switch between looking and changing. In Edit, click anything on the page to change it, or ask Row-Bot about it; double-click text to edit it in place. Changes save as you go. - **Undo** and **Redo** step through your changes; **Versions** lists saved versions and restores one. - The **page strip** moves between pages, adds a page after the current one, or deletes one. - **Size** chooses the canvas (16:9 widescreen, 4:3, square, A4 document, 9:16 phone, or a custom size). **Device width** previews pages at desktop, tablet or phone width, and the zoom control fits or scales the page. - **Present** shows the design full screen. - **Share** publishes a link (with a QR code), sends to a channel, or prepares an X post. - **Export** saves the current saved version as **PDF**, **PNG**, **PowerPoint** (pictures for high fidelity, or editable text and shapes) or **HTML**, for all pages, the current page or a page range. - The **** menu opens the design command palette to search tools, pages and assets, imports a document, or duplicates the design. ## The Inspector **Inspector** opens three tabs: - **Selection** edits the chosen element: its text, font, size, weight, colour and alignment; an image's file, fit, crop, corners and description; width and borders; and what happens when it is clicked (go to a screen, toggle a state, play media). **Edit as CSS...** is there for exact control. - **Brand** sets the design's **Colours** (primary, secondary, accent, background and text), **Fonts** for headings and body from a font picker (recently used, bundled, and fonts on this computer), and the **Logo**: upload one, then choose its placement, size, spacing, which pages show it, and automatic or manual placement. Save the brand as a preset to reuse it in other designs. - **Library** inserts **Blocks**, **Your images**, saved **Styles** and **Interactions**. **Review** checks the design and lists what to fix. ## Brand And Media Providers Generated images or videos call the image and video models chosen in **Settings Models**. Local design edits stay in local project data. For xAI API image models, Row-Bot uses the provider's live image-generation catalog instead of guessing from the chat catalog. It exposes only the formats, aspect ratios, resolutions, and quality choices reported for that model. If xAI rejects an optional quality field, Row-Bot retries once without it; timeouts and other failures do not trigger an automatic second generation that could duplicate cost. ## What Is Saved Designs, their versions and brand presets are local Row-Bot data. Deleting the conversation keeps the design; open it from another conversation with **Add resource... Open saved**. ## Troubleshooting - If a first draft is thin, give a clearer goal, audience and length, and attach references. - If an export looks wrong, preview each page first; exports use the last saved version. - If image generation is unavailable, choose an image model in Settings Models and check its provider. - If a change says the design changed meanwhile, let the panel reload the current version and try again.

## Code Folders

Route: /docs/developer/

Work on a folder or repository from a conversation: bind or clone it, review changes, run checks and use Git in the Developer panel.

# Code Folders A code folder is a folder or Git repository on this computer that a conversation works on. Bind one to a conversation and Row-Bot can read its files, propose and make edits, run checks and commands you approve, and help with Git. The folder opens in the conversation's **Developer panel**, beside the chat. ## Bring A Folder Into A Conversation **Ask in the chat.** Row-Bot binds folders by itself when you ask: - "Use my Hello-World folder" binds a code folder you already use, by its name. If several names match, a **Which code folder?** card lets you choose; if none does, a **Use an existing folder** card asks you to choose the folder on this computer. - "Clone https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World" shows a **Clone a repository** card with the address. Choose **Choose where** to pick the parent folder, and Row-Bot clones it there. An interrupted clone is kept for inspection and offers **Check clone status**; it is never cloned again automatically. Either way, the conversation shows a **Using code folder ...** card with **Open** and **Undo**. The turn pauses while a card waits for you and continues in the folder once it is bound. Row-Bot never chooses a path on its own: you choose every folder in the picker. **Or set it up yourself.** Open the composer's **+** menu, choose **Add resource...**, then **Code folder**: | Folder setup | What it does | | --- | --- | | **New draft in the configured workspace** | Creates an empty folder under Drafts in your workspace folder. | | **Register an existing folder** | Saves an existing folder's name and location; its files and Git state are unchanged. | | **Create a new empty folder** | Creates one empty folder under a parent you choose. | | **Clone a repository** | Downloads a repository into a new folder under a parent you choose. | **Open saved** brings a code folder you used before into this conversation. Home Overview's **New code folder** does the same in a new chat. Choosing a folder on this computer needs the Row-Bot desktop app. The conversation's details card lists the folder under **Working on**. Its **** menu, or **Undo** on the card, unbinds it from the conversation; the files stay on disk. The Agents tool can also assign a child directly to an existing local folder. Row-Bot validates the path and registers it as that child's code folder; a folder assignment and a pre-existing workspace ID are alternative ways to select the workspace, not settings to combine. ## The Developer Panel - **Changes** lists changed files with their diffs (unified or split), and the agent's own change sets, each marked reviewed or not reviewed, with **Undo** or **Ask Row-Bot to undo** in its **** menu. - **Files** browses the folder and previews files. - **Run** lists the checks Row-Bot detected (such as tests and linters) with their last result, runs a command you type (such as `npm test`) as a reviewed command, shows running processes with their output, and stops them. Sandbox changes waiting to be imported appear here too. - **Git** switches or creates branches, commits with a suggested message, pushes (which asks first), opens a pull request through the GitHub command-line tool, and creates a separate worktree for this conversation. - **Safety boundaries** shows what is allowed, what asks first and what is blocked here, where commands run, and whether the sandbox has network access. - **Custom tools** turns the folder's commands into a reusable tool with the Custom Tool Builder. Your custom tools are also listed in **Settings Tools Custom tools**. ## End-To-End Workflow 1. Bind or clone the folder in a conversation. 2. Check the folder name, branch and changes in the panel. 3. Ask a question about the code, or describe the change you want. 4. Approve only the commands and edits you understand. 5. Run the checks from **Run**. 6. Review **Changes** before committing, then commit and push from **Git**. ## Parallel Child Workspaces Writer ownership follows the resolved workspace folder. Children working in distinct folders or worktrees can edit concurrently, while writers aimed at the same folder are serialized to prevent overlapping changes. Changing only a shell working directory does not create an independent write boundary. Use a separate worktree or folder when two children genuinely need parallel write access. ## Sandbox Modes Local mode lets Row-Bot operate in the selected workspace with your configured file and command permissions. Docker Sandbox mode, when available on a host installation, isolates command execution in a container and requires an import step before changes affect the real workspace. It requires a supported host Docker runtime and can differ from your local environment. Inside the official Row-Bot application container, Developer Docker Sandbox is unavailable and a requested Docker workspace fails closed; Row-Bot never probes a nested daemon or silently runs that workspace locally. Local mode remains an explicit choice and can see only workspace paths deliberately mounted into the application container. An approved risky Custom Tool is a third case: it deliberately executes in Local mode inside the application container against the selected visible Custom Tool path. That behavior is shown in the approval dialog and is not a nested Docker sandbox or fallback from a requested Docker workspace. See [Docker And VPS Operations](/docs/operations/docker#developer-and-headless-boundaries) for the complete container boundary. For a host installation, start with Local mode on a disposable branch. Use Docker Sandbox when you want stronger isolation and the supported host runtime is available. ## Troubleshooting - If Row-Bot can't see your code, check that the folder is listed under **Working on** in the conversation's details card. - If choosing a folder does nothing, use the Row-Bot desktop app; a browser can't open folders on this computer. - If an Agent folder assignment is rejected, confirm that the directory already exists and pass either that folder or an existing workspace ID, not both. - If a command asks for approval, read the exact command and folder before approving. - If Docker sandbox import is offered, review the patch before importing it into the real project.

## Knowledge

Route: /docs/knowledge/

Explore, search, review and correct what Row-Bot remembers in Home Knowledge, and configure memory in Settings Memory.

# Knowledge Knowledge is Row-Bot's local memory: the facts, people, projects, preferences and relationships it has saved from conversations, documents and your own edits, connected as a graph. Row-Bot recalls relevant memories when they help a conversation. For the relationship between thread history, memory, documents, the graph, Wiki Vault, and Dream Cycle, read [How Memory Becomes Knowledge](/docs/concepts/memory-knowledge-and-dream-cycle). ## Where To Find It - **Home Knowledge** is where you see and manage memories. - **Settings Memory** turns memory on or off, shows graph health, configures the [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault), and holds **Delete all knowledge**. - **Settings Documents** configures document search and its embedding model. ## Views Choose a view at the top of the Knowledge tab: - **Graph** draws memories and their connections and lets the layout settle into place. It opens with up to 2,000 memories; **Show all memories** draws up to 5,000. Use **Zoom in**, **Zoom out** and **Fit**, and hide or show memory types from the legend. - **List** shows the whole library, newest first, with search across every memory. - **Review** is the queue of memories Row-Bot was unsure about. **Mark as reviewed**, **Edit memory** or **Archive memory** settles each one. - **Activity** shows recent recalls (memory used or skipped in a conversation) and recent changes. **Filters** narrow the graph and list by source, status and memory type, show or hide you as the central memory, and can hide unconnected memories. ## A Memory's Details Select a memory to see its description, memory type, status, source, confidence and when it was updated, its connections, where it came from, and its history (created, edited by you, refined by Row-Bot, last recalled). From there: - **Edit memory** corrects it. - **Merge or replace** folds a duplicate into another memory and moves its connections. - **Archive memory** keeps it but stops it being recalled; **Restore memory** brings it back. - **Delete memory** removes it, its connections and its search entries after you confirm. Select several memories to delete them together, up to 100 at a time. Use **Add memory** to save something yourself. ## Dream Cycle Dream Cycle tidies memory overnight: it merges duplicates, enriches thin memories and infers missing links. Turn it on and choose its hours in **Settings Preferences Overnight tidy-up**. **Run Dream Cycle** on the Knowledge tab reviews what it would do and runs it now after you confirm. Its history is in [Monitor](/docs/monitor/). ## Common Workflow 1. Open Home Knowledge after a few useful chats or document imports. 2. Search for the topic you care about, or open **Review**. 3. Open a memory and check its source. 4. Correct, merge, archive or delete misleading memories. 5. Rely on recall once the important memories are right. ## What Is Saved Memories are local Row-Bot data. They are sent to a model provider only as relevant context in a conversation that uses that provider. ## Troubleshooting - If Knowledge is empty, turn on memory in Settings Memory or add documents in Settings Documents. - If a memory is wrong, edit, merge or archive it rather than deleting whole topics. - If recall feels noisy, review the **Review** queue and archive stale memories. Continue with [Wiki Vault](/docs/knowledge/wiki-vault) and [Provenance And Repair](/docs/knowledge/provenance-repair) for the file-output and recovery workflows.

## Wiki Vault

Route: /docs/knowledge/wiki-vault

Keep a local Markdown vault of Row-Bot's memories, with readable file names, and sync your edits back.

# Wiki Vault Wiki Vault writes your memories and their connections as linked Markdown articles in a folder you choose, so you can read them in Obsidian or any editor. It is an output of the local knowledge graph, not a replacement for the underlying memory and provenance records. ## Configure The Vault 1. Open **Settings Memory** and find **Wiki vault**. 2. Turn on **Enable Wiki Vault** and choose the vault folder with **Browse**. Choosing a folder needs the Row-Bot desktop app; pick a folder separate from application code and important personal notes while you test. 3. Save the configuration, then use **Rebuild managed wiki files** to write every article. 4. Open the articles in your editor and check links, titles and source notes. Articles have readable names: a memory called "Garden plan" becomes `Garden plan.md` in the folder for its type. When two memories share a name, or a note of your own already uses it, Row-Bot adds a short code to the new file name instead of overwriting anything. A renamed memory's article is renamed with it. ## What Row-Bot Writes And Leaves Alone Row-Bot keeps a record of the articles it wrote and only ever updates or moves those. Notes you create yourself in the vault are never changed or deleted. Articles from an earlier version are adopted in place with the same names, so existing links keep working. Files Row-Bot replaced are moved aside for your review, not deleted; **Show moved files** lists them. ## Your Edits When you edit an article in the vault, **Sync vault edits** brings the change back to the memory. If the memory changed in Row-Bot too, **Resolve versions** lets you choose between the database version and the vault version. Correct important facts in Knowledge first when you can, so the graph remains the source of truth. ## Privacy The vault is local, but it is deliberately easy to open in other software or sync with a third-party folder. Treat the destination as an export boundary. Review it before placing it in cloud storage, a shared repository, or a publishing system. ## Troubleshooting - If articles are missing, check that memory is on and the vault folder reads **Available**, then rebuild. - If **Browse** opens no folder picker, use the Row-Bot desktop app; a browser can't choose folders on this computer. - If links duplicate, run Knowledge repair before rebuilding the vault. - If private material appears, correct or remove its source memory, rebuild, and review the destination before sharing.

## Knowledge Provenance And Repair

Route: /docs/knowledge/provenance-repair

Trace where knowledge came from, correct records, repair relations, and rebuild derived outputs safely.

# Knowledge Provenance And Repair Knowledge is useful only when you can tell where it came from. Review provenance before relying on a memory, document fact, entity, or relation for consequential work. ## Review A Record 1. Open **Home Knowledge** and search or filter to the topic. 2. Select the memory to open its details. 3. Check its source, timestamps, type, confidence or status, and related entities. 4. Compare important claims with the original conversation or document. 5. Correct, merge, or remove the record if it is misleading. ## Repair Order Use the smallest repair that fixes the problem: 1. Correct a title, type, description, or relation. 2.
